notes.1: Same App. C.3.3 at two issues: pre-2024 says the unknown-acute-toxicity statement is required 'on the label'; the 2024 text adds '(oral/dermal/inhalation)' and 'and safety data sheet'. Added requirement, same provision - not a simultaneous conflict.
notes.10: Same legend entry in the organic-peroxide available-oxygen formula at two issues: 'DHc = chemical heat of combustion' vs 'DHc(product) = specific heat of combustion ... of the product'. Same symbol and same quantity, reworded (verified against eCFR title 29 point-in-time snapshots).
notes.15: Same pH-based serious-eye-damage paragraph: old A.3.3.1 vs 2024 A.3.2.2.4; renumbered cross-reference plus a tightened confirmation clause ('further evaluation may be necessary' -> 'needs to be confirmed by other data, preferably ... validated in vitro test'). Same rule at two issues.
notes.28: Same respiratory/skin sensitizer cut-off table; 2024 adds the caption and moves '%' into the column headers. Values identical.
notes.37: Different endpoints: 'Table A.9.1 - Guidance Values To Assist in Category 1 Classification' is the STOT repeated/prolonged exposure table, while 'A.8.2.1.9 Guidance Values ... for Category 1 and 2' is STOT single exposure. Shared title words only.
notes.49: Two different tables of the same appendix that coexist in the same issue: Table A.1.1 (category cut-offs, e.g. oral <=5 mg/kg) and Table A.1.2 (conversion of an already-classified range to an ATE point estimate, e.g. Category 1 -> 0.5). A range endpoint and a derived point estimate are not the same measured quantity, so the overlapping digits are not a quantity conflict; both tables can be true at once.
notes.53: Same table template, different hazard classes: germ cell mutagen cut-offs vs specific target organ toxicant cut-offs. No shared subject.
notes.56: Same Table B.13.1 (criteria for oxidizing liquids) with the caption added in the later rendering; criteria text identical.
notes.61: Table B.12.1 sits inside section B.12 in the same issue ('Chemicals Which, in Contact With Water, Emit Flammable Gases'); the table is a part of the section, and both are true.
notes.70: Same paragraph at two issues: old A.2.2.2.2 vs 2024 A.2.2.2.2.4 (the 2024 rule pushed skin irritation down two levels under 'A.2.2.2 Classification Based on Standard Animal Test Data'); only 'might/could' -> 'should' wording changed.
notes.80: Same explosives paragraph (f) at two issues: 'items which contain only extremely insensitive detonating chemicals' -> 'items which predominantly contain ...'.
notes.88: Not parent/child: pre-2024 App. A section A.2.2.2 is headed 'Irritation'; in the 2024 text that same irritation content is A.2.2.2.2 'Skin Irritation' (with A.2.2.2.2.1-.4 = old A.2.2.2.1-.3). Same provision renumbered down two levels.
notes.157: Different subjects within 29 CFR 1910.120: passage A is the training-curriculum text (App. E, 'Basic core requirements for training programs'), passage B is spill-containment/permit-exception prose followed by the App. D 'References' list. The shared standard number is incidental.
notes.165: Both passages are current 40 CFR 112 text, not two issues of one rule: A is 112.3(b)(4)(i) (a Tier II qualified facility may not self-certify alternative measures; a licensed PE must certify them), B is 112.4(c) (a nonconforming facility states reasons for nonconformance and describes alternate methods in the Plan). Different scopes, and a facility can satisfy both - state the reasons and obtain PE certification - so nothing is irreconcilable.
